title: Indicator: Stochastic — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #12 (indicator-stochastic), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: _validate_period's int/bool/range guard in stochastic.py duplicates the identical inline check in app/indicators/ema.py::ema(). force_index.py avoided this by delegating to ema() directly, but stochastic.py can't (it's SMA-, not EMA-, based) — extract a shared _validate_period-style helper once a third indicator needs the same check, rather than a third copy-paste.

decisions.decision: Extracted the duplicated int/bool/range period-validation guard from app/indicators/ema.py::ema() and app/indicators/stochastic.py::stochastic_oscillator() into a new shared app/indicators/_validation.py::validate_period(name, value) helper, and had both call sites delegate to it. This was done now even though only two duplicates exist, not three as the checklist item's own text said to wait for.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's stated precondition ('extract... once a third indicator needs the same check') was explicitly overridden by direct user instruction: a maintained, non-duplicated implementation was judged worth doing immediately rather than waiting for a third copy-paste to accumulate. The refactor is behavior-preserving — same error types, same parametrized error-message wording (stochastic.py's existing _validate_period(name, value) signature was reused as the shared helper's signature so ema.py's call site, which validates a single param literally named 'period', produces byte-identical error text to before) — verified via each indicator's existing test suite plus new direct tests for the helper in tests/unit/indicators/test_validation.py. Rejected keeping the module-level function name with its leading underscore (_validate_period) in the new shared module: the module itself (app/indicators/_validation.py) already signals package-internal-only via its own leading underscore, so the function name didn't need a second one now that it's called from outside its original module.

comments.summary: Confirmed pure, behavior-preserving refactor: diffed against the original PR #12 state and the new shared app/indicators/_validation.py::validate_period() is byte-for-byte identical logic to both call sites' prior inline guards (isinstance(value, bool) / isinstance(value, int) check, value < 1 check, identical error text via the caller-supplied name). ema.py and stochastic.py's actual computation (ewm/rolling math) is untouched. All call sites of ema()/stochastic_oscillator() pass fixed valid literal periods, so this is invisible to every caller.

Task's decisions entry correctly documents the explicit user override of the checklist item's own stated 'wait for a third indicator' precondition, with rationale covering why (avoid a third copy-paste accumulating) and the rejected alternative (keeping the leading-underscore name in the new module).

Backend test suite: 493 passed, 0 failed. Coverage 99.84% overall (app/indicators/_validation.py itself at 100%), well above the 90% gate. No ruff/mypy configured in backend/pyproject.toml, so no lint/typecheck step applies.

No UI-facing changes in this PR (backend-only: two indicator modules, a new validation helper, its unit tests, and task-board JSON) — browser walkthrough is not applicable and was skipped explicitly rather than silently.

Non-blocking: docs/architecture/Backend.md §2's module layout listing under indicators/ doesn't mention the new shared app/indicators/_validation.py helper module (placement itself is fine — pure function, no I/O, package-internal via leading underscore — just a doc-staleness gap). Tracked as a follow-up task (indicator-stochastic-followups-followups) rather than left only in this comment.

review.notes: Verified this is a genuine behavior-preserving refactor by diffing the pre-refactor state (PR #12, commit adf3b58) directly against the post-refactor state (commit 7b39da4): identical error types, identical error-message wording per call site, identical range check. No indicator math changed, so docs/Analyse.md's methodology sections (tide/wave/trigger/impulse/confidence/risk) don't intersect this change at all. code-review skill (medium effort) found zero findings. architecture-review found the module placement itself sound but flagged the Backend.md §2 doc-staleness gap noted above (tracked as a follow-up, non-blocking). No API/schema changes, so no OpenAPI snapshot concern. No pre-existing pr_decision on this task to clear.
